text:
kevin: Heads up — last hour we saw a sharp queue growth in us-west1, warm pool depleted and admission started returning 503s. Noticing more cross-region fallthroughs than usual. Anyone oncall?

nina: Saw it too. Warm pool went from ~80 -> 8 in ~6m. Part of that traffic looks like a partner stress test hitting multiple routes. Autoscaler showed no prewarm because acct-3 hit NIC/instance quotas in us-west1-b.

sam: oncall. Collecting logs now. autoscaler-bot shows instance create delayed ~90s with "Quota exceeded for network interfaces" errors. Link: https://go/reports/1976543210/logs

elaine: NIC quota is weird — we had buffer for bursts. @kevin do we know if this is cloud quota or something in our provisioning path? :thinking:

kevin: Cloud NIC quota in us-west1-b is the immediate blocker. Raised a quick ticket with cloud support but need short-term mitigation. Suggestion: implement a "soft-admit" policy that avoids hard rejects by reducing per-request concurrency (smaller batch sizes) and shedding large multi-request batches instead. Keeps requests live, increases latency a bit but avoids 503s.

tariq: Proposal sounds reasonable. Example trade-offs: fewer tokens per batch -> more per-token overhead and cost, but better user-facing errors. Also we can selectively enable for public tiers.

sam: Draft config I sketched for canary:
```
{
  "policy": "soft_admit_v1",
  "conditions": "warm_pool_fill < 0.15 || pending_queue > 250",
  "reduce_batch_factor": 0.5,
  "max_inflight_per_customer": 3,
  "min_warm_pool_reserve": 5,
  "fallback_model": "llama-2-13b-q4"
}
```
This would shrink batch sizes and cap per-customer concurrency before returning hard rejects.

nina: Couple of concerns: 1) cost could spike due to more small inferences; 2) model switching/fallbacks could introduce quality/regression noise. We should gate by customer tier and region.

kevin: Agreed. Plan: gate soft_admit to non-enterprise customers and only allow cross-region fallbacks for enterprise. Also set a cost budget alarm.

sam: Also noticed network flapping in us-west1-b causing some pods to hit startup timeouts during prewarm. We should add a 30s backoff and retry for prewarm attempts, and mark AZ unhealthy if NIC throttle persists > 3 attempts. That reduces churn for the autoscaler.

autoscaler-bot: scaled up 4 g4dn-equivalent GPUs in us-west1-c (eta ~110s) :white_check_mark:

elaine: I'll push a canary rollout at 10% traffic for soft_admit_v1 and add new metrics: admission_rate, avg_batch_size, warm_pool_fill, cross_region_fallbacks. Proposed alert: admission_rate > 2% for 10m => pager.

tariq: I'll open the PR with the policy + rollout plan and include a simulated runbook for quota exhaustion. Tagging @kevin @nina for review.

kevin: :thumbsup: thanks all. Monitor costs and latency closely during canary and be ready to kill the rollout if warm_pool_fill doesn't improve within 20m or if error budget burns.

infra-bot: note: created incident INC-1976543210 for quota/exhaustion; linking ticket CT-9982 to this thread.
